answer.rationale:
Diagnosis first: the two measured declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are upstream of everything else. The competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal but memory_73 says discounting buys acquisition at the direct cost of retention, which is the opposite of the primary objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue), so promotional_pricing is rejected on the stated objective rather than on appetite. Referral incentives (memory_57) work in established customers and do nothing for a top-of-funnel activation decline; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is real but addresses a segment that is not the one deteriorating. That leaves simplify_onboarding and activation_messaging, both plausible; simplify_onboarding is chosen because it attacks the earlier failure point, and a completion recovery should partially propagate into activation, whereas messaging fixes only the later stage.

I am spending the verification budget on the two memories my chosen action actually rests on, not on the ones I already decided against. memory_31 (day 12) and memory_86 (day 52) are suspiciously convergent: one says cutting required fields lifted SMB activation, the other says shortening onboarding lifted adoption. These may be two independent findings, or memory_86 may be a re-consolidation/echo of memory_31, in which case my apparent double support collapses to a single 64-day-old result from a possibly different market condition. That distinction changes the scale of the commitment, so it is worth the budget. I am also treating both as inherited summaries whose original effect sizes, segments, and durations I have not seen.

Flagged downstream risk: the specific mechanism in memory_31 is removing required signup fields. Those fields plausibly feed lead qualification and routing into the demo-request path that memory_44 identifies as the higher-quality enterprise pipeline. A change that improves self-serve activation numbers while quietly degrading enterprise routing would raise the metric and lower qualified revenue, which is exactly the failure the primary objective forbids. So the experiment must be scoped to SMB self-serve traffic, must leave enterprise-intent paths untouched, and must carry pipeline-quality and downstream retention as guardrail metrics, not just completion rate.

Contingency, stated before seeing the archive: if verification shows memory_86 is independent of memory_31 and both used comparable segments, I run the standard experiment as scoped. If memory_86 turns out to be derived from memory_31, or if either record shows a short measurement window or a segment unlike today's, I downscale to a small guarded test and treat the prior as one aging data point rather than a replicated finding. I am not treating the inherited summaries as settled fact.
